records.name: Pennypack Ecological Restoration Trust
records.summary: Stewards of Pennypack Park, a long green corridor in the Northeast. Volunteers pull invasive vines off trees, help with restoration projects alongside staff, and join a Presidents Day service morning each February.
records.what_you_do: Free-A-Tree workdays cut invasive vines off trees on the first Saturday of the month, October through April. Service Day mornings work on an active restoration project with staff. Bring gloves and pruning shears, or borrow theirs.

schedule.text: Free-A-Tree workdays on the first Saturday of each month, October through April. A Service Day runs around Presidents Day (the 2026 one was Monday, Feb 16, 10 am to 12 pm).

locations.label: Pennypack Park, Philadelphia (trail and restoration work; specific sites vary)
Trust headquarters
locations.address: 2955 Edge Hill Road, Huntingdon Valley, PA 19006

cost.text: Not stated on the pages read

first_step.how: Register through the Trust's volunteer sign-up link before the date (Free-A-Tree and Service Day both ask for pre-registration), or call the office at 215.657.0830
first_step.basis: The Trust says volunteers learn restoration from staff, says groups and individuals are welcome, and publishes a sign-up link.

records.notes: Trust office is in Huntingdon Valley (Montgomery County). Its trails and work sites are in Pennypack Park, which runs into Philadelphia, but some work may be outside city limits, so check before going. The Service Day page gives its start as 10 pm in one spot and 10 am in another; 10 am is used here and should be confirmed. Streamkeepers and ReForesters programs are named on the site but were not read. Cost not stated on the pages read. Friends of Pennypack Park is listed in leads_only.

records.name: Oxford Circle Christian Community Development Association
records.summary: A faith-based nonprofit serving Oxford Circle. It runs an after school and summer camp, adult education and job help, food distribution, and a Wednesday farmers market at Castor Avenue and Hellerman Street.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer with children, adults, or other tasks (the group says it welcomes volunteers), or shop at the Wednesday farmers market. The newsletter carries event news.

schedule.text: Farmers market on Wednesdays, 11 am to 3 pm, at Hellerman Street and Castor Avenue (per a 2025 market listing; confirm the 2026 season). Camp and class schedules are not posted on the site.

cost.text: Not stated on the pages read

first_step.how: Call (215) 288-8504 or email contact@occcda.org, or use the Volunteer Today link on the website. The farmers market is a public Wednesday event.
first_step.basis: The market is open to the public and the office lists ways to volunteer, but the sign-up steps for camp and classes are not published.

records.notes: The group's site lists after school and summer camp, adult education and workforce development, family resource centers, food distribution, Parents as Teachers, and business corridor work, but gives no current dates for them; the newest dated item on the site is a 2021 summer camp. Farmers market hours come from a 2025 market listing and the market page itself gives no hours. The group calls itself Christian and faith-based, but no faith requirement is stated, so the faith field is blank. Northeast Passage (classes for immigrants and refugees) is named in search results as a program here; its Mural Arts page returned 404, so it is not recorded separately. The Exchange thrift shop address was not confirmed from a readable page, so it is not used.
